I should trust more the details page in general? for older blocks at least right? both change. the logic should be equal 😄 let me check 🙂 ah yeah it shows differently now lodestar-geth-1 managed to sync from genesis, we should be voting properly on all nodes now, thanks for checking that beautiful and bad at the same time, we have a bug that makes us propose on full when empty should have won, I think <@363800010518822915> is investigating it, but now triggering it will be harder 🙂 ping on this one, this is something that the spec is rather lacking. It's one of the odd consequences of having to deal with payload equivocations Hi <@&1417820113981145228> has anyone run into the following scenario? When calling `is_parent_block_full` on the beacon state at the first Gloas slot, the function returns true even though the last Fulu block had no full payload. This happens because `UpgradeToGloas` initializes both `latest_execution_payload_bid.block_hash` and `latest_block_hash` to the same (the last Fulu EL hash), so the equality check in is_parent_block_full is satisfied spuriously. Does this break anything for your internal caching We designed that function so that it returns true at the fork <@737658693331714159> ran into this issue when working on fork choice i think Yes `is_parent_block_full` should be true at first gloas slot. Our internal caching treats all pre-gloas blocks to be FULL variants anyways Yup I’m assuming all pre-Gloas blocks to be FULL as well. Since we have variants for ProtoNode. we have some sort of a hybrid because we didn't want to change the fact that we use blockroots to access pre Gloas poststates so we still treat them as empty but in some places they are naturally treated as full We could just move to treat them entirely as full, but that seemed like a more dangerous change to merge now in develop

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Hi <@&1417820113981145228> has anyone run into the following scenario?  When calling `is_parent_block_full` on the beacon state at the first Gloas slot, the function returns true even though the last Fulu block had no full payload. This happens because `UpgradeToGloas` initializes both `latest_execution_payload_bid.block_hash` and `latest_block_hash` to the same (the last Fulu EL hash), so the equality check in is_parent_block_full is satisfied spuriously.  Does this  break anything for your internal caching

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: We designed that function so that it returns true at the fork
